Instruction funnel shares; operationalisation rate; evaluation coverage; per-instruction compliance rate (share of applicable commits in which the instruction is followed), by category and agent; extraction precision/recall/F1 and label accuracy; script spot-check agreement

Automatic: Qwen 3.5 9B annotator (local, temp 0.1) extracts instructions with few-shot prompt; manual validation of 84 snapshots by one author; Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct generates 10 scripts + 10 fixture pairs per instruction (CodeT-style, temp 0.8), accepted if passing >= 2 fixtures and >= 60% corroboration; manual spot-check of 94 scripts; scripts run on before/after files of applicable commits (applicability from fixture file patterns). Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney U with Bonferroni, Cliff's delta, sensitivity at >= 3 and >= 5 commits

Observational, per originating agent (ACF + agent; models not stated); metric: per-instruction compliance rate with its own ACF on applicable commits; no success criterion stated by the authors. - ACF + GitHub Copilot + model n.s.: 1,137 instructions evaluated (coverage 48.0%); mean 66.0%, median 100%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors. - ACF + Claude Code + model n.s.: 799 evaluated (52.6%); mean 52.2%, median 66.7%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors. - ACF + OpenAI Codex + model n.s.: 117 evaluated (49.6%); mean 51.2%, median 100%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors. Overall: mean 59.8%, median 100%; 54.4% of instructions always followed, 37.3% never, 8.3% in between. Cost: not measured

fields.v: No controlled comparison: real commits mined; groups compared by category (18) and originating agent (3) using one compliance rate per instruction. No baseline (no counterfactual without instruction). Not held constant: repositories, languages, category mix differ across agents. Acceptance: generated scripts (71.3% correct on spot-check). Repetitions: N/A. Sensitivity analysis on thin-evidence instructions

Category differences significant (H = 59.13, p < .001); four pairs after Bonferroni: Development Process lower than Build and Run (delta -0.39), Documentation (-0.29), Implementation Details (-0.32); Implementation Details > Testing (0.15). Only ImplDetails vs Testing survives at >= 3 and >= 5. Agent differences significant (H = 41.58, p < .001): Copilot > Claude Code (delta 0.15, robust), Copilot > Codex (0.13, full sample only); Claude Code = Codex. Operationalisation by agent 62.1-63.5%; by category, among the 12 categories with >= 50 instructions, 47.7% (Management) to 75.6% (Config and Environment) (all 19: 0% AI Integration, 1 instruction, to 90.9% General, 11)

rev.why: The category range 47.7-75.6% holds only for the twelve categories with at least 50 instructions (p. 18); Table 6 includes General 90.9% and AI Integration 0%, so the range without the qualifier was wrong

fields.v: Partly: pipeline operationalised 62.9% of observable instructions, but only 31.3% of them produced a compliance observation; 28.7% of accepted scripts wrong on spot-check; permissive defaults (62.3% of scripts return True without evidence) make compliance optimistic; agent effect is association only (category mix not controlled)

No counterfactual (compliance may reflect defaults); snapshot-commit linking; agent comparison not controlled for category mix; authorship attribution noise; stochastic LLM components; acceptance thresholds from a pilot; scripts see final file state not diff; binary compliance; single annotator; open-weight local models; public GitHub only, three agents. Future: more agents, causes of gaps, enforcement at generation time; recommend artefact-checkable rules and tooling (hooks, CI) for process conventions
